newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi working to open economy - deputy finmin.
newsitem.headline: Saudi working to open economy - deputy finmin.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is working to open its oil-dominated economy and encourage foreign investment, cut its deficit and give the private sector a bigger role, its deputy finance minister said on Wednesday.

"The kingdom has shown a strong determination to further liberalise its economy, keep inflation under control, reduce the government deficit, increase the role of the private sector, reduce reliance on oil and encourage foreign investment," said Deputy Finance and National Economy Minister Jobara al-Suraisry.
Speaking at the Gulf Economic Forum in Bahrain he said gross domestic product (GDP) at current prices grew an estimated 8.6 percent in 1996 from 4.3 percent in 1995.
Suraisry did not give real GDP but said "there is viturally no inflation in the economy", adding the cost of living index rose by less than one percent last year.

He said the government budget deficit had declined to 18.5 billion riyals ($4.93 billion) in 1996 from 62 billion riyals in 1993. In 1996, the budget deficit was 3.6 percent of GDP compared with 11 percent in 1993, he added.
"The current account deficit has fallen steadily from over 27 billion Saudi riyals in 1991 to a 700 million Saudi riyal surplus in 1996," Suraisry said.
He said the kingdom had doubled its allocation for education to 41 billion riyals and allocated 17.8 billion riyals for health and social development in 1997.
"This is only an example of the strong determination of the government...to build up the country's human resources and skills," he added.
Another 8.6 billion riyals had been allocated for infrastructure this year and 11 billion riyals of new electricity power projects have been approved, Suraisry said.
The kingdom is the world's biggest oil exporter and producer, producing around eight million barrels of oil per day.
